items.title: Why Do Moving Bodies Shrink? The Physical Origins of Length Contraction
items.description:
Do bodies in motion truly, physically contract? And if so, how does this happen? Turns out, you don't need Einstein's Theory of Special Relativity to explain it. Here indeed we present a first-of-its-kind derivation of the phenomenon of Length Contraction from purely physical, classical wave-mechanics principles, without any use of any spooky space or time relativity. Join us as we pull back the curtain and expose the workings behind one of nature's most mysterious phenomena...

global_silver_linings.snippet: A record 30,000 coho salmon returned to central California rivers last season—up 10x from an average of 3,000 over the last decade—and double the total of last season. Running up the rivers which empty into the Mendocino coast, the proliferation among the fish is something that scientists studying the animals thought they’d never see in […] The post Endangered Salmon Return to California Rivers in Incredible Numbers: ‘Everybody’s just ecstatic’ appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: After years of habitat loss and drought, the return of endangered salmon to California rivers in remarkable numbers is a powerful sign that nature can rebound when given a fighting chance. The sheer joy in that quote reminds us that conservation work, however slow and unglamorous, genuinely pays off.

discovery_articles.title: Who Knew Illinois Had This Many Spooky Places?
discovery_articles.snippet: Illinois is known for its haunted houses and Halloween extravaganzas: the kinds of places that draw lines out the door and attract visitors from all over the country. But beyond these creepy crowd favorites are a number of lesser-known spooky spots, all with backstories both historical and paranormal—like the “devil baby” that haunts a former Chicago settlement house or the witchy tomb that draws in fans of the occult from far and wide. The Prairie State is home to all manner of legendary urban myths and strange characters whose life stories sound too far-fetched to be true, until you realize they just might be … With spooky season underway, there’s no time like the present to explore Illinois’s many odd and eerie destinations.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: The 'devil baby' rumor that haunted Hull House — Jane Addams's own settlement — was so persistent that desperate visitors knocked on the door for weeks demanding to see it, forcing Addams to write an entire essay just to address the legend. Illinois's strangeness runs deeper than any haunted hayride.

discovery_articles.title: A New York City Exhibition Celebrates Snoopy’s Enduring Influence on Art and Fashion
discovery_articles.snippet: The beloved "Peanuts" character’s many costumes and brand collaborations are featured in a new showcase
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Snoopy has quietly become one of the most collaborated-upon characters in fashion history, lending his beagle silhouette to luxury houses and streetwear alike — proof that a dog who sleeps on a rooftop has impeccable taste. Charles Schulz drew him as an everyman; the world dressed him as an icon.

discovery_articles.title: Kermit the Frog Was Just Trying to Put on a Variety Show. Fifty Years Later, the Muppets Are Some of the Biggest Stars in Television History
discovery_articles.snippet: The first episode of Jim Henson's "The Muppet Show" premiered in the United Kingdom on September 5, 1976. Enthusiasm for the eclectic ensemble has endured ever since
discovery_articles.ferns_note: What's easy to forget is that *The Muppet Show* was originally rejected by every American network — it took a British syndication deal to give Kermit his stage. Fifty years on, the show that no one wanted is the one everyone remembers.

discovery_articles.title: After an Eight-Year Journey, Two Spacecraft Have Begun Their Arrival to Mercury, the Inner Solar System's Most Mysterious Planet
discovery_articles.snippet: The BepiColombo mission, by the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, is only the third to study our smallest planetary neighbor
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Mercury is so close to the Sun that studying it requires spacecraft to brake against solar gravity rather than accelerate toward it — a counterintuitive, years-long falling act that makes BepiColombo's arrival almost as remarkable as the planet itself. Only two missions have ever made it there before.

news.title: Meera Sodha’s vegetarian recipe for kacang pool, or Malaysian bean stew
news.snippet: A delicious and triumphant blend of Levantine and Malay cuisines This is a dish with roots in ancient Egypt. There, it started life as ful medames , the famous fava bean dish lightly seasoned with cumin, garlic and lemon. Then it was, reportedly, brought to Johor in Malaysia by Arab traders.
news.blurb: A dish that wandered from ancient Egypt to Malaysia and back again — Meera Sodha's kacang pool is the kind of culinary crossroads story that makes you hungry for both history and dinner.

recipe.title: peach cobbler loaf
recipe.snippet: A friend asked me last week how long it takes to get a recipe right. I told him the only answer I know: As long as it takes. I’d like to be someone who could “adjust my expectations,” make peace with “close enough,” or have the slightest amount of chill when it’s clear that whatever I’m trying to do isn’t something I can pull off, but we’re wired how we’re wired.
recipe.blurb: A loaf cake built around peak-summer peaches, this cobbler-inspired bake is the sort of unhurried weekend project that makes your kitchen smell like the best possible version of August.
